newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: WHO confirms cholera in eastern Zaire.
newsitem.headline: WHO confirms cholera in eastern Zaire.

text.p: Fourteen hospital patients in Goma who came from the eastern Zaire village of Sake have been confirmed as having cholera, the World Health Organisation (WHO) said on Friday.

Maria Neira, a Spanish doctor who heads WHO's global task force on cholera, reported the laboratory results to a news briefing following a WHO mission to the region. "For the first time, laboratory tests have confirmed that it is cholera."
"The patients came from Sake, so this confirms there is a big epidemic. It is frustrating and very worrying," WHO's Neira later told reporters.
"We don't know what is happening in Sake. We appeal to be able to reach these people and give them medical assistance."
The Geneva-based United Nations health agency feared outbreaks of other epidemics, including bloody diarrhoea known as shigella, according to the expert.

The exact condition of the 14 patients, believed to all be Zaireans, was not known, according to Neira, who is heading to Kigali on Sunday. All were receiving good care and most had stabilised when the WHO doctor left Goma earlier this week, although two were suffering from extreme dehydration.
